ov: Plant-eating insects camouflaged as sticks or leaves, found on every continent except Antarctica, most of all in the tropics. They are nocturnal, feeding under leaves at night and keeping still by day. Some species are the world’s longest insects.

why.p: Almost 300 species have been reared as pets or in labs, and they have been pets since China's Han dynasty.
why.ac: Nocturnal, feeding under leaves at twilight or midnight and keeping still by day.

rg: Worldwide except Antarctica and Patagonia; over 300 species live on Borneo alone.
df: Leaves; the Indian stick insect kept as a pet eats vegetables such as lettuce.
fx: Almost 300 species have been reared in laboratories or as pets; in China they have been kept since the Han dynasty.
Some sway from side to side to mimic a twig moving in the breeze.
